Pricing/GTM posture: position assistant‑lite as included for enterprise customers for this narrow, auditable domain to compete with Competitor Y’s bundle, while labeling expansions as future, paid roadmap milestones; prefer pilot discounts over permanent bundling to avoid a price race.  
Next steps I recommend: run a two‑week UX sprint to deliver the diff prototype, assign one senior engineer to the hardening work, update Sales materials and the demo checklist with the tightened messaging, and get CTO/CFO sign‑off tonight to lock scope for the RFP/demo.

Edits and provenance will also be preserved for record maintenance, and short pauses won't trigger refunds unless they materially affect service levels. rounds.response:
Recommend these rollback/throttle conditions (key assumptions): 1) sustained breach of critical performance SLOs or systemic latency impacting users; 2) verified data‑integrity/provenance failures or corrupted/unsourced snapshots; 3) confirmed security incidents or model behavior producing harmful/misleading outputs; 4) regulatory/legal orders or a customer admin request requiring immediate disable.  
If the assistant is paused, customers keep full access to core dashboards, scheduled one‑pager exports, and historical snapshots/audit logs (admins can export or delete these records); edits and provenance remain preserved and downloadable so QBRs and records are intact; recommend that short tactical pauses not automatically trigger refunds, while prolonged or widespread disabling that meaningfully reduces contracted service levels be handled case‑by‑case with pro‑rata credits or renewal concessions per an incident remediation policy to be finalized.  
Board language (lift‑ready): “We run a disciplined, auditable assistant with explicit performance, security and legal gates—pauses are a supported safety mechanism and do not erase your historical snapshots or audit trails; we will only replicate the assistant pattern after objective SLOs, measured pilot ROI and operational readiness are met,” underscoring how this approach mitigates risk versus ‘AI everywhere’ plays.
